correctness.rationale: Coordinatewise squaring in the graphical evolution algebra is T=A sigma with binary adjacency A commuting with Frobenius. Hence T^j=A^j sigma^j and kernel sizes are (2^f)^(N-rank A^j). Fitting decomposition into A's stable image U and nilpotent kernel V identifies periodic states as U and gives the exact by-j preperiod count. A normal basis turns sigma into an f-slot cycle; the gcd(m,f) slot-orbits impose A^lcm(m,f) v=v, proving the fixed-point rank formula even for singular A. For a complete multipartite graph A=E C S with S E=D, and C D C block ranks give rho1, rho2 and stable rho3; stable dynamics is sigma on odd-part hyperplane or (I+J)sigma on even-odd-part coordinates, giving the stated o-parity fixed-point law and sharp maximum periods. Independently checked the K_(1,1) F4 versus F8 fixed point counts via field Frobenius and swap, and reviewed the actual complete-state enumeration program; its small test cases are not used as an infinite proof.
